key_insight: Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) fuse the complexity-aware scheduling of autoregressive methods with continuous, iterative latent refinement to allocate computation where it's needed, producing high-quality images faster and without lossy discrete tokenization.
problem_solved: Addresses the uniform, costly sampling of diffusion models and the discrete-token and error-accumulation limitations of autoregressive models by enabling adaptive, region-aware refinement in continuous latent space.
method: Iterative continuous-latent refinement: a network predicts residual corrections in latent space rather than discrete tokens, reducing quantization loss and accumulation of discrete errors.
Complexity-aware scheduler: learns per-sample and per-region uncertainty/likelihood to allocate more refinement steps to harder regions while skipping easy ones, enabling adaptive compute.
Hybrid objectives and consistency regularization: combine reconstruction, perceptual, and temporal/consistency losses to stabilize multi-step refinements and preserve fidelity.
impact: GRN enables faster, more compute-efficient image synthesis with quality comparable to state-of-the-art while avoiding tokenization artifacts — useful for deployment in resource-constrained or real-time generation settings and for researchers exploring adaptive inference.

paper_title: Generative Refinement Networks for Visual Synthesis
paper_authors: Jian Han, Jinlai Liu, Jiahuan Wang, Bingyue Peng, Zehuan Yuan
